thread_text:
1. Failure is essential

Amazon's Panay says failure is essential — but why? He credits his toughest defeats as biggest lessons.

2. Defeats become lessons

He credits his toughest defeats as biggest lessons. That's not just talk — it's how Amazon innovates.

3. Most companies punish failure

Yet most companies punish failure, not reward it. Employees learn to play it safe, killing innovation.

4. Your safe failure budget

Your next project needs a safe failure budget. Set aside resources for experiments that might fail.

5. Track one failure this week

Track one failure this week; learn from it. What will you try that might not work?

instagram.caption:
Getting fired is the fastest way to learn, says Amazon's devices chief Panos Panay.

He credits his toughest defeats as his biggest lessons — not just talk, but how Amazon keeps innovating.

Most companies do the opposite: punish failure, so employees play it safe and innovation dies.

If you make or publish anything, give your next project a safe failure budget — resources for experiments allowed to flop.

Track one failure this week. What will you try that might not work? 💡
